question: Which article of the Constitution abolishes 'Untouchability'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 17**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 17** of the **Constitution of India** specifically deals with the **abolition of untouchability**. It states that "Untouchability" is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. ***Hence, Article 17 is the correct answer.***
 
• This article ensures that the enforcement of any disability arising out of **"Untouchability"** shall be an offense punishable in accordance with the **law**.
 
• It is a significant provision under **Part III** of the Constitution, which covers **Fundamental Rights**, aimed at establishing social equality and dignity for all citizens, especially those from marginalized communities.
 
• Unlike many other fundamental rights, **Article 17** is **absolute** in nature, meaning no exceptions are provided for its violation under any circumstances.
 
• The **Parliament** of India, exercising its power under **Article 35**, enacted the **Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955**, which was later renamed the **Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955**, to prescribe punishments for practicing untouchability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 14**:

 
 
• This article guarantees **Equality before the law** and **Equal protection of the laws** within the territory of **India**.
 
• It prohibits **discrimination** and ensures that the state shall not deny any person equality. However, it does not specifically mention the abolition of untouchability. ***Hence, Article 14 is an incorrect option.***
 
 
 
• **Article 19**:
 
 
• This article protects **six fundamental freedoms** for the citizens of India, including freedom of **speech and expression**, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• These freedoms are subject to **reasonable restrictions** in the interest of the sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, etc. ***Hence, Article 19 is an incorrect option.***
 
 
 
• **Article 21**:
 
 
• This article provides for the **Protection of Life and Personal Liberty**. It states that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to **procedure established by law**.
 
• The **Supreme Court** has expanded its scope to include the right to **privacy**, right to clean environment, and right to education. ***Hence, Article 21 is an incorrect option.***
 
 
 
• **Article 15**:
 
 
• While not in the primary options, it is related as it prohibits discrimination on grounds only of **religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth**.
 
• It specifically provides access to **shops, public restaurants, hotels, and places of public entertainment** to all citizens.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context**: The inclusion of **Article 17** was a direct response to the centuries-old social evil of untouchability in India. **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, the father of the Indian Constitution, was a leading proponent of this provision.
 
• **Terminology**: Interestingly, the word **"Untouchability"** is placed within quotation marks in the Constitution because it is not defined in the Constitution or the Act. Courts have interpreted it to mean the social practice as it developed historically in India.
 
• **Enforcement Acts**:
 
 
• **Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955**: Provides penalties for preventing a person from entering a place of public worship or taking water from a public well/tank.
 
• **Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989**: This act was passed to prevent atrocities against members of **SC and ST** communities and to provide for special courts for the trial of such offenses.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Right**: Article 17 is enforceable not just against the **State** but also against **private individuals**. It is the duty of the State to take necessary steps to ensure this right is not violated.
